tasks.title: The only control that can clear missing ids is hidden when the catalog is empty
tasks.body:
## Confirmed defect

`modelsDropMissingBtn.hidden = modelsCatalog.length === 0;` (static/admin.js:8421) hides the Remove-missing control exactly when discovery returned an empty catalog, so every saved id is missing, no checkboxes exist, bulk actions are disabled and Save cannot be enabled by a selection change. The operator cannot clear the filter through the replacement UI.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/../static/admin.js:8421`
- Source PR: #322 (closed, merged=true), original head `c17a5d9057d942b79c038d9f8f19e0d7fb871952`, merge `610f203132d4b01b4f4bb3741eb8db7546ad7d16`

## Original review finding

P2 `The only control that can clear missing ids is hidden when the catalog is empty` - reported against `static/admin.js:8300` by native review turn `01a0fca1-2006-7ef0-8031-339118d6cf0d` (thread `01a0fca1-1122-7fe1-b341-cfee336916f5`) for PR #322.

## Trigger / reproduction

Static source read at `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` shows the cited code path unchanged; the exact expression is named above. No runtime, browser, or production operation was performed to confirm this.

## Acceptance

The Remove-missing control must remain available when discovery returned an empty catalog and every saved id is missing, so the operator can clear the filter. Add a focused test or minimal relay for an empty catalog with saved ids.

## Evidence and duplicate check

- Reviewer head `98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502`; validated against `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (source-only static read).
- For merged PRs the current upstream default-branch head was compared with the reviewer head; every file cited here is either absent from that comparison's changed-file list (byte-identical) or was re-read at the current head.
- Duplicate check (2026-10-02): all open and closed issues in `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi` were paginated in full (120 issues); no existing issue covers this trigger.

tasks.title: In-band Lithos refusals overwrite their classified health event with upstream_error, so /health/providers reports degraded
tasks.body:
## Original finding (same defect, two cited sites)
- Native Codex review of PR #515, finding 3: [P2] Preserve provider-health classification for deferred refusals (original cite lithos-handlers.ts:577-579). Native Codex review of PR #514, finding 3: [P2] Preserve refusal-specific provider health (original cite lithos-streams.ts:126-127).
- PR #515 original head 96c52bed9af1cdaff7db427111ffc1010912e097; PR #514 original head f9c9f4542f9acf97f7b2216628a1d08709905704. Provenance as in CAND-AI-RELAY-01.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; all four files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- refuseStream records the classified refusal and then the generic provider error, in both relays: stream-relay.ts:189-190 (Chat) and 459-460 (Responses) call recordResponseHealth(detail.status) and then recordProviderError(detail.status).
- The Lithos adapter maps classified statuses deliberately (lithos-streams.ts:86-108: 401/403 -> auth_invalid, 402/429 -> quota_exhausted), but recordProviderError unconditionally records upstream_error (lithos-streams.ts:127).
- The dispatcher already classified the same refusal before handing the streamed Response to the relay (lithos-handlers.ts:193-207 respondLithosChatUpstreamHttpFailure records the classified health and failure kind; the deferred and immediate streamed paths pass that Response into the relay at lines 596-613 and 833-845).
- Health writes are serialized per provider+identity in arrival order (health.ts:184-205) and the newest observation decides the state (health.ts:284-303: upstream_error -> degraded, quota_exhausted -> exhausted, auth_invalid -> invalid), so the generic observation wins.

## Trigger
1. A streamed or deferred Lithos request ends in an HTTP 429/402/401/403 refusal that is relayed in-band.
2. The refusal path records quota_exhausted or auth_invalid.
3. The relay's refuseStream then records upstream_error for the same refusal.
4. /health/providers shows degraded instead of exhausted/invalid, so admin and routing diagnostics lose the refusal-specific signal.

## Acceptance
- Do not let a generic provider-error observation overwrite an already classified refusal on the in-band relay path (for example skip recordProviderError when the refusal carried a classified status, or route classified refusals through a dedicated seam).
- Regression test: streamed 429 and 401 refusals leave /health/providers at exhausted and invalid respectively, with the last observation still classified.

## Duplicate search (fresh, 2026-10-02)
- Corpus scan (596 issues): provider-health terms return 42 hits; the newest are #576/#585/#596/#597 and none describes a classified refusal being overwritten by the relay's generic callback. #601 (local quota refusal masked as an OpenRouter upstream failure) is a different provider and path.
- Fresh GitHub search q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+rate_limit_failover_model / failover+window / refuseStream -> only the reviewed PRs.
- No existing or audit-filed issue matches (all open and closed issues in this repository were paginated in full).

## Labels
Time: <2 Hours; Priority: 2 (Medium) - existing labels only (fully paginated label list, 44 labels).

Validation: static source/control-flow inspection at the current revision above; no runtime inference or repository test was executed.
